record.original_question: Given a function kappa in C^-1(0,+infinity), what conditions are necessary and sufficient for kappa to belong to the class L1 of Sonine-kernel pairs, and how can one derive an explicit representation of the associated kernel k that satisfies the Sonine relation (kappa * k)(t) = 1 for t > 0?

evidence.quote: The set of such Sonine kernels is denoted by L1: (kappa, k in L1) iff (kappa, k in C^-1,0(0, +infinity)) and ((kappa * k)(t) = {1}).
For a function kappa in C^-1(0, +infinity), determine the conditions for the inclusion kappa in L1 and derive a representation for the associated kernel k.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ denote the space of functions $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ that are continuous on $(0,+\infty)$ and satisfy $f(t)=t^{p}f_1(t)$ for some $p>-1$ and some $f_1\in C[0,+\infty)$. Let $C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$ be its subspace consisting of those $f\in C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ with $p<0$ (so that $f$ has at most an integrable power-type singularity at $0$). For $f,g\in C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ define the Laplace convolution
$$(f*g)(t)=\int_0^t f(t-\tau)g(\tau)\,d\tau,\qquad t>0.$$
A pair $(\kappa,k)$ of functions in $C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$ is called a Sonine pair, written $(\kappa,k)\in\mathcal{L}_1$, if it satisfies the Sonine condition
$$(\kappa*k)(t)=1\quad\text{for all } t>0.$$

Problem. Given a function $\kappa\in C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$:
(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on $\kappa$ for the existence of $k\in C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$ such that $(\kappa,k)\in\mathcal{L}_1$, i.e.\ for $\kappa\in\mathcal{L}_1$.
(b) Under these conditions, derive an explicit representation formula for the associated Sonine kernel $k$.
artifact.category_tag: Sonine kernels and general fractional calculus
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing Sonine kernel pairs in the class $\mathcal{L}_1$ has been studied within Luchko's general fractional calculus framework, where partial results give sufficient conditions (e.g., kernels with integrable power-type singularities, via Laplace-transform criteria) and explicit examples (power, Mittag-Leffler-type kernels). A complete characterization in the full class $C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ together with a general explicit representation of the associated kernel does not appear to be settled in the literature surveyed; the status is therefore unclear.

status_evidence.title: General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives with the Sonine Kernels
status_evidence.snippet: A class of Sonine kernels that possess an integrable singularity of power function type at the point zero has been introduced; fundamental theorems are proved for general fractional integrals/derivatives with kernels from this class.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient conditions and a working subclass for Sonine pairs are established, but a full characterization in $C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ is not given.

status_evidence.title: Sequential generalized Riemann–Liouville derivatives based on distributional convolution
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the Sonine condition $(\kappa*k)(t)=1$ and pairs $(\kappa,k)\in\mathcal{L}_1$ within $C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the framework used in the question but does not resolve the general characterization problem.
